content.value_statement: Web teams need a repeatable way to check common application risks before release. This skill organizes OWASP testing into phases, prompts, and reporting steps.
actual_capabilities: Structures web application testing into reconnaissance, injection, XSS, authentication, access control, headers, and reporting phases.
Lists focused checks for OWASP Top 10 coverage and quality gates.
Provides copy-paste prompts for related security testing skills.
Guides documentation of vulnerabilities, proof of concepts, risk levels, and remediation.
Helps coordinate specialized testing skills during an authorized assessment.
limitations: Does not run scanners or execute tests by itself.
Requires explicit authorization and a defined testing scope.
Depends on other referenced skills for detailed exploit checks.
Does not replace expert review of findings and legal constraints.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Web App Assessment
use_cases.description: Plan the testing phases, target areas, and expected evidence for an authorized web application review.

use_cases.title: Check Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Use the OWASP checklist to confirm key controls before a production release.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Bug Bounty Triage
use_cases.description: Organize valid reports by vulnerability class, risk level, proof, and remediation status.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Test Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for an authorized review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an OWASP web security test plan for this application. Include phases, scope notes, evidence to collect, and reporting checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Review Authentication Controls
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate assessment of sign-in and session behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess authentication and session management risks for this application. Focus on lockout, MFA, session expiry, password policy, and test evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Map Access Control Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an access control test matrix for these roles and endpoints. Include vertical escalation, horizontal escalation, IDOR checks, and expected results.

prompt_templates.title: Produce an Executive Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these validated web security findings into a concise report. Include impact, severity, proof summary, affected areas, remediation, and retest guidance.

output_examples.input: Plan a security test for a customer portal before launch.
output_examples.output: A phased checklist covering reconnaissance, injection, XSS, authentication, access control, headers, evidence collection, and final reporting.

output_examples.input: Summarize validated access control issues for stakeholders.
output_examples.output: A clear report section with affected roles, business impact, reproduction summary, severity rationale, and remediation steps.

output_examples.input: Check whether OWASP Top 10 areas were covered.
output_examples.output: A coverage review showing tested categories, missing evidence, unresolved questions, and next actions before signoff.

best_practices: Define written authorization, scope, rate limits, and test windows before starting.
Record evidence, affected assets, reproduction steps, and remediation owners for every confirmed issue.
Retest fixes and update the report with verified outcomes.
anti_patterns: Testing systems without permission or outside the approved scope.
Reporting scanner output without manual validation and impact analysis.
Skipping documentation of assumptions, test limits, and unresolved risks.

faq.question: Does this skill execute security tools?
faq.answer: No. It provides a workflow and prompts for coordinating authorized web security testing.

faq.question: Can I use it for production systems?
faq.answer: Yes, only with explicit authorization, defined scope, and safe testing limits.

faq.question: Which vulnerabilities does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers OWASP Top 10 areas, including injection, XSS, authentication, access control, misconfiguration, and SSRF review.

faq.question: Does it replace a penetration tester?
faq.answer: No. It helps organize work, but expert validation is still required.

faq.question: Can it help with reporting?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes reporting steps for impact, risk, proof, remediation, and retesting.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
